sources.publisher: United States Congress / House History, Art & Archives
sources.title: WARREN, Elizabeth: congressional biography, education and Senate terms
sources.findings: Read the congressional biography. It identifies a Massachusetts senator, born in Oklahoma City on 22 June 1949, with a Houston B.S. in 1970 and Rutgers J.D. in 1976; attendance at George Washington University is not a degree. It confirms 2008–2010 oversight-panel chairmanship, Senate service beginning 3 January 2013 after the 2012 election, re-elections in 2018 and 2024, and unsuccessful pursuit of the 2020 Democratic nomination. The House-hosted biography does not imply House membership. The term ending in January 2031 is a scheduled endpoint, not a completed tenure. Do not adopt an imprecise nationwide third-place primary ranking from raw encyclopedic evidence.

sources.title: Committee assignments for the 119th Congress
sources.findings: Read the 119th Congress assignments. Warren is the Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee ranking member, not its chair, and is also assigned to Finance, Armed Services and Aging. This current page takes precedence over older faculty-page committee lists. Policy priorities including taxation, competition, drug costs and retirement security are positions, not proof that particular bills became law. Do not infer a 120th Congress chairmanship from election speculation.

sources.title: 17 September 2010: appointment as Assistant to the President and Special Advisor to the Secretary of the Treasury
sources.findings: Read the archived 17 September 2010 White House appointment. Her titles were Assistant to the President and Special Advisor to the Secretary of the Treasury, leading the CFPB setup. Congress and the President established the agency through legislation; it was not created by a unilateral act of Warren. Her appointment was not confirmation as the agency’s first director. Historical counts of books and articles are not current totals.

sources.publisher: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau / Treasury Department
sources.title: 26 July 2011: leadership transition effective 1 August and proposed first director
sources.findings: Read the 26 July 2011 Treasury transition release hosted by CFPB. Raj Date was to succeed Warren as special advisor effective 1 August, while she would return to Harvard; announcement and effective dates differ. It identifies Richard Cordray as the president’s intended nominee for the first director role, not a Senate-confirmed director already serving that July. A June 2026 webpage modification date does not redate the 2011 transition. The release also confirms the agency’s creation under Dodd–Frank in July 2010.

sources.title: Elizabeth Warren: emerita faculty biography and academic appointments
sources.findings: Read the Harvard faculty biography. It lists the current emerita title, a 1992–1993 visiting commercial-law appointment and the 1995 permanent Leo Gottlieb appointment. Research includes bankruptcy, commercial law, contracts and empirical work on household financial stress. Teaching at Harvard is not a Harvard degree or deanship; emerita is not an honorary doctorate. The older Senate committee list and book count are not treated as current. A broad institutional account of her role in CFPB advocacy is refined by the contemporary appointment and transition sources.

sources.title: 17 November 2026: Armed Services nomination-hearing transcript and questions about war costs
sources.findings: Read the release and actual-exchange transcript, both dated 17 November 2026, of the Armed Services hearing involving Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao and his nomination. Warren personally questioned war/blockade costs and urged action through appropriations. Avoid the internally difficult-to-reconcile daily/monthly/aggregate cost figures and do not present her legal or political characterisations as judicial findings. Proposed spending reallocations are not approved budgets. The transcript is supplied by her office; the linked video was not viewed.

sources.title: 15 August 2022: Warren accepts lifetime membership; undergraduate field of study
sources.findings: Read the Massachusetts Speech-Language-Hearing Association’s 15 August 2022 notice of accepted lifetime membership. It supports the Houston undergraduate field of speech pathology and audiology, with degree level/year corroborated by Congress. It cites secondary biographies rather than a university transcript. Lifetime association membership is not a degree or proof of a current clinical licence. Personal recollections about an early teaching job are not independently established employment findings here.

sources.title: 9 February 2019: formal presidential campaign launch in Lawrence, Massachusetts
sources.findings: Read ABC’s 9 February 2019 account of the formal campaign launch in Lawrence for the 2020 presidential nomination. The campaign year differs from the election year. Dynamic 2026 election widgets above the article are unrelated to this 2019 event and were excluded. Campaign crowd estimates, ancestry controversy and opponents’ accusations are not needed for the dossier and are not adopted as verified membership, ethnicity or misconduct findings.

sources.title: 5 March 2020: Warren suspends presidential campaign
sources.findings: Read ABC’s 5 March 2020 account of the suspended campaign, corroborated by Congress’s unsuccessful-nomination record. Not endorsing another candidate that day does not mean she never endorsed one later. A third-place finish in a particular contest is not a national final ranking. Proposed wealth-tax rates and projected revenue are campaign proposals, not enacted nationwide taxes or observed receipts; no amounts are carried into the profile.

sources.title: 13 November 2026: letter urging General Motors to change its stock-buyback plans
sources.findings: Read the 13 November 2026 office release describing the letter to GM and its request for a response by 25 November. That future response deadline is not evidence of a response already received. Requests to abandon buybacks or reinvest are advocacy and oversight, not binding regulatory orders or a verified company reversal. The release’s claims about taxation, layoffs, tariffs and corporate motives are not adopted as independent findings. The linked letter PDF and company financial records were not separately inspected.

sources.title: 16 January 2025: first hearing as Banking Committee ranking member
sources.findings: Read the 16 January 2025 office release and opening-remarks transcript. It records her first hearing as Banking Committee ranking member, with Tim Scott chair, during Scott Turner’s housing-secretary nomination process. This is the first-hearing date, not necessarily the date she was appointed to the committee role. Questions and priorities do not establish enactment, confirmed misconduct by unnamed landlords or Turner’s confirmation that day. Linked video/livestream not viewed.

sources.title: 21 November 2008 report of the 14 November Congressional Oversight Panel appointment
sources.findings: Read Harvard’s 21 November 2008 report identifying the appointment to the five-member Congressional Oversight Panel on 14 November. Membership appointment is distinct from later election as chair, which the congressional biography dates within 2008–2010. The panel scrutinised Treasury’s TARP and reported to Congress; it did not make Warren the personal administrator of bailout funds. The academic article’s publication date is not the appointment date, and its projected future reports are not described as already delivered.

portraitReview.unresolved: Read the cropped Commons page, its linked parent file and original Flickr description. They identify Warren speaking at Laney College, Oakland, on 31 May 2019. Flickr upload was 3 June 2019; the full 4124×2749 photo was transferred to Commons by SecretName101 on 6 June, with FlickreviewR 2 confirming CC BY-SA 2.0 that day. Gindomarlo uploaded cropped revisions on 13–14 January 2020; the current crop is 1538×2035. The 2020 media timestamp is not the photography date, and uploaders are not substituted for Gage Skidmore as photographer. Attribution, licence link, change indication and share-alike requirements remain applicable. Original cropped JPEG download on 18 November returned curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000; the referenced cached JPEG is absent. No image pixels viewed, so identity, original colour, crop suitability and correspondence with the full frame remain unverified.
